title: ICE deports former Colts linebacker Daniel Adongo over expired visa
content:
Federal immigration officials announced Saturday they have deported former Indianapolis Colts linebacker Daniel Ogama Adongo, who allegedly overstayed his visa.

Adongo, a former professional rugby player from Kenya who entered the NFL with no American football experience, appeared in games for the Colts in the 2013 and 2015 seasons. As an outside linebacker, he played 100 special teams snaps and one snap on defense, and was the league’s first Kenyan player.

ICE said in a statement that Adongo, 36, overstayed his visa after the Colts waived him in 2015. It said a Department of Justice immigration judge ordered Adongo’s removal March 23, and he was removed from the country June 20.

Adongo experienced a series of legal issues in Indiana starting in February 2015, most of which involved civil disputes and vehicle violations, such as expired license plates. He faced two felony charges in 2020 for “intimidation where (defendant) draws or uses a deadly weapon” and for criminal mischief resulting in damage between $750 and $50,000. The first charge was dismissed as part of a plea deal, and Adongo was sentenced to six months in county jail.

ICE cited that case as grounds for Adongo’s deportation, pointing to the Laken Riley Act, which requires the agency to detain undocumented immigrants who have been arrested in connection with burglary, theft, larceny, shoplifting or assault cases. The agency did not explain which category Adongo’s case falls under, but ICE can detain someone who was arrested or charged with a qualifying offense, even if they were never convicted.

“This dangerous individual was clearly a threat to the community, which is now safer since he’s been removed,” said Douglas Thompson, ICE Chicago assistant field office director, in the statement. “Those who violate immigration law are held equally accountable, including former professional athletes.”

Adongo later faced misdemeanor charges in 2022 and 2025 in alleged intimidation, disorderly conduct and battery cases, though those cases were all dismissed.

It’s unclear whether ICE returned Adongo to Kenya or sent him elsewhere. Whether he currently has legal representation is also unknown. ICE did not respond to The Athletic’s request for comment.
